title: Similarity All The Way Up: Multilingual Generalization in LLMs Relies on Language-Level Similarity Structures
abstract: arXiv:2607.22699v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: As Large Language Models (LLMs) grow more capable across diverse tasks, their (in)ability to generalize remains difficult to quantify and poorly understood beyond limited domains. In particular, LLMs are known to struggle generalizing multilingually, to languages outside of English, and that are poorly attested in their training data. To understand why this may be, and what enables some models to perform better than others, we turn to a long history of work across the cognitive sciences, arguing that successful generalization derives from appropriate representations in similarity space. We look at how well LLMs' representations capture the hierarchical similarity structure between distinct languages. Strikingly, we show LLMs' latent representations largely recover the hierarchical structure of the Indo-European language family tree -- grouping languages that are members of the same subfamily closely together in representation space.

translated_title: 相似性贯穿始终：大型语言模型的多语言泛化依赖于语言级相似性结构
translated_abstract: 摘要：随着大型语言模型（LLMs）在各种任务上能力不断增强，它们的（不）泛化能力仍然难以量化，且在有限领域之外理解不足。特别是，已知LLMs在多语言泛化方面存在困难，即对英语以外的语言以及训练数据中覆盖不足的语言。为了理解这一现象的原因，以及是什么使某些模型比其他模型表现更好，我们回顾了认知科学领域的长期研究，认为成功的泛化源于相似性空间中的适当表征。我们考察了LLMs的表征在多大程度上捕捉了不同语言之间的层级相似性结构。引人注目的是，我们展示了LLMs的潜在表征在很大程度上恢复了印欧语系语言家族的层级结构——将属于同一亚语系的语言在表征空间中紧密地分组在一起。
tldr: 本文发现大型语言模型通过恢复印欧语系的层级相似性结构来支持多语言泛化，表明语言级相似性是跨语言表现的关键因素。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that LLMs support multilingual generalization by recovering the hierarchical similarity structure of the Indo-European language family, highlighting language-level similarity as a key factor in cross-lingual performance.
